reasons: The principle of converting the C3 dwelling to a 5-bedroom HMO is considered acceptable: the property provides suitable internal accommodation and communal facilities, the rear area can accommodate waste and recycling bins, the site is sustainably located within walking distance of Doncaster city centre and public transport, the accommodation would be limited to five occupiers, the site is in Flood Zone 1, and the proposal would not result in an over-concentration of HMOs. The proposal accords with Policy 9 of the Doncaster Local Plan.

The proposal would preserve the character and appearance of the area because no external alterations are proposed and the internal alterations, including removal of the existing chimney, would not affect the external appearance. The development would respond positively to the existing context and accords with Policies 41 and 44 of the Doncaster Local Plan.

The proposal would provide acceptable living conditions for future occupiers and would not cause unacceptable harm to neighbouring residential amenity. All bedrooms exceed the 10sqm guidance standard, the layout, kitchen and bathroom facilities are adequate, private rear amenity space would remain, and there would be no demonstrable harm from overlooking, daylight loss, outlook loss or noise given the nature of the change of use and absence of external alterations. The proposal accords with Policies 44 and 45 of the Doncaster Local Plan.

The proposal is acceptable in highway and parking terms. Although no off-street parking is provided, this reflects the existing situation, on-street parking is available nearby, the site is sustainably located, and the Highway Officer raised no concerns; the development would not have a demonstrable impact on parking or the highway network and accords with Policy 13 of the Doncaster Local Plan.

Waste management arrangements are considered acceptable for planning purposes because the rear garden provides space for domestic-scale waste storage with access to the rear alley for collection, and waste management would also be addressed through HMO licensing.
conditions: The development must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of this permission. Reason: Condition required to be imposed by Section 91, as amended, of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development hereby permitted must be carried out and completed entirely in accordance with the terms of this permission and the approved plans: Plan number 9 - LR - 103, Location plan and site plan, received 09/03/2026; Plan number 9 - LR - 104, Proposed elevations, received 09/03/2026; and Plan number 9 - LR - 103, Proposed floor plans and roof plan, received 09/03/2026. Reason: To ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the application as approved.
The maximum number of tenants/residents to be housed at the property shall be no greater than five. Reason: To ensure that the facility is not detrimental to residential amenity.
